purpose: Evaluation only; never imported by application code

sources.title: London Daily rate article from original assessment
SELECT primary trial abstract; not full text

cases.claim: SQLite WAL permits concurrent reading and writing and therefore SQLITE_BUSY cannot occur.

elements.description: WAL permits concurrent reading and writing.
SQLITE_BUSY cannot occur in WAL mode.

cases.review_guidance: Check both directions from the same source. Locate the BUSY exception beyond the lead. Review its exact context, not just a heading.

cases.claim: SQLite WAL permits concurrent reads and writes, but SQLITE_BUSY remains possible.

elements.description: WAL permits concurrent reading and writing.
SQLITE_BUSY can occur in WAL mode.

cases.review_guidance: Reversal control: the same exception should support the possibility; never force a challenge because the prior case had one.

cases.claim: SQLite version 3.22.0 relaxed the restrictions on opening read-only WAL databases.

elements.description: Access remains subject to documented conditions.

cases.review_guidance: Retain version, conditions and release date. Two pages from the same documentation do not become two independent experiments.

cases.claim: As of 7 September 2026, Bank Rate was 3.75% and the next decision was scheduled for 17 September 2026.

elements.description: The next decision as of that date was scheduled for 17 September 2026.

cases.review_guidance: Historical motivating input, not a current truth assertion. New homepage bytes cannot reconstruct yesterday automatically. Review whether source dates actually establish the target period. Undated contrary text and header clocks do not establish a live contradiction; apply symmetrically. Do not infer applicability from domain.

cases.claim: As of 7 September 2026, Bank Rate was 4.25%.
cases.review_guidance: Reversed numeric control over identical sources. Judge temporal evidence rather than agreeing with the submitted number. May remain unestablished if the saved texts cannot establish that date.

cases.claim: SELECT proves heart-attack prevention in everyone overweight, with a 20% absolute reduction.

elements.description: SELECT establishes prevention for everyone overweight.
The reported primary outcome is heart attacks alone.
The reported reduction is 20 percentage points.

cases.review_guidance: Separate study population, composite endpoint and effect measure. Review actual trial data; do not treat failure to establish a universal claim as proof of no benefit. FDA summary and primary abstract describe one underlying trial.

cases.claim: SELECT studied a composite cardiovascular outcome in a defined population and reported a relative rather than 20-percentage-point absolute reduction.

elements.description: The studied population has specific inclusion criteria.
The primary endpoint combines multiple cardiovascular outcomes.
Relative and absolute effect measures differ.

cases.review_guidance: Opposing control using the identical study texts. Review endpoint, comparator, population, follow-up and effect metric independently; preserve genuine favourable findings.

cases.claim: These SQLite documents establish that copper bracelets prevent dementia.
cases.review_guidance: No relationship control. Retrieved text does not establish this health claim. Do not force mappings or fabricate a study; no medical advice is requested.
